sources.entry: Runner - Open-source workspace where CLI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, and pi work one task together as a crew, each in its own real terminal. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/yicheng47/runner) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Runner is an open-source workspace where terminal coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Copilot CLI work on one mission together as a crew, each in its own real terminal.
keywords: agents work together on a task
summary.what_it_does: Runner lets you compose saved agent roles into reusable crews and launch a mission in which each crew slot runs its own live terminal session. A shared mission feed lets the agents coordinate and raise questions to the user, and individual slots can be stopped, resumed or restarted without affecting the others. Each agent keeps its native TUI in a real PTY rendered on a GPU-drawn alacritty_terminal grid, with split tabs, windows, a shell drawer and IME input. A runner command-line interface can start chats, launch crews and follow missions, with JSON output and an installed skill for detected agents. Sessions run in a background service called runnerd, so agents keep running when the app is closed, and stopped agents resume their conversations on the next launch. The README also describes MCP server and skill management per agent, desktop notifications, project working directories, and a remote-control feature in private beta.
use_cases: run several coding agents on one task at once
coder and reviewer agent pairing with a review loop
manage Claude Code and Codex sessions in one window
launch repeatable agent teams from the command line
get notified when a coding agent needs input
keep agent sessions alive after closing the app
how_to_run: runner mission start --crew "Pair coding crew" --goal-file brief.md
stack: GPUI (Zed's GPU UI framework, via gpui-pre)
notable: Coordinates multiple third-party CLI agents in real terminals rather than wrapping their APIs, so each agent keeps its own TUI
Reusable crews with a default Pair coding crew example (coder plus reviewer, both on Codex by default)
runnerd background service keeps sessions alive across app quit or crash
runner CLI with --json output, usable by scripts and by agents themselves
Per-agent MCP and skills settings that change only the entry touched
caveats: Alpha status; native macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows (x64) builds, Linux only in beta and verified only on one Ubuntu 26.04 ARM64 VM
Remote control is invite-only private beta, currently available in mainland China
Features and platform support vary by agent; TRAE CLI is opt-in only
